questions.question: During which Five-Year Plan was the focus on 'Self-reliance' particularly emphasised?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Third Five-Year Plan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Third Five-Year Plan** (1961-1966) focused heavily on achieving **self-reliance** in various sectors, particularly agriculture and industry.
 
• This plan aimed at making India self-sufficient in the production of food and reducing dependency on imports for essential goods and resources.
 
• The emphasis on **self-reliance** was driven by the challenges of foreign exchange reserves and the need for economic independence.
 
• Under this plan, there was a significant thrust on increasing **domestic production** capabilities by investing heavily in agriculture, infrastructure, and basic industries.
 
• The plan was disrupted by the **Indo-China war (1962)** and the subsequent economic crisis, but it laid the groundwork for India's long-term focus on self-sustainability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **First Five-Year Plan (1951-1956):**

 
 
• Focused primarily on **agriculture** and aimed at resolving food shortages caused by Partition and World War II.
 
• Major investments were made in irrigation, dams, and land reforms.
 
• The success of this plan was evident in increased agricultural production.
 
 
 
• **Sixth Five-Year Plan (1980-1985):**
 
 
• The Sixth Plan focused on **poverty alleviation**, infrastructure development, and rural employment.
 
• This marked the beginning of the **Integrated Rural Development Programme (IRDP)**.
 
• It also emphasized improving living standards and reducing inequalities between rural and urban areas.
 
 
 
• **Ninth Five-Year Plan (1997-2002):**
 
 
• This plan aimed at **economic growth** with social justice and equity.
 
• It focused on improving **human development indices** like education, health, and employment.
 
• The plan attempted to integrate economic reforms with developmental objectives.
 
 
 
• **Indo-China War (1962):**
 
 
• Occurred during the **Third Five-Year Plan**, leading to an economic disruption.
 
• India faced increased defense spending, which impacted the planned allocation of resources for development.
 
• Despite the war, the emphasis on **self-reliance** remained intact as a cornerstone of India's economic strategy.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Self-reliance:**

 
 
• Refers to the ability of a country to meet its own economic needs without heavy reliance on external sources.
 
• It includes **domestic production** of food, industrial goods, and essential resources.
 
• Key sectors involved in achieving self-reliance include **agriculture, manufacturing, and infrastructure development**.
 
 
 
• **Five-Year Plans in India:**
 
 
• India's Five-Year Plans were introduced in **1951** to promote planned economic development.
 
• These plans were formulated by the **Planning Commission**, which was replaced by the **NITI Aayog** in 2015.
 
• Each plan focused on specific objectives such as poverty alleviation, industrial growth, and infrastructure improvement.

questions.question: Part-IV of the Constitution of India states about which of the following?

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of water body?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Delta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **delta** is a landform created at the mouth of a river where it flows into an ocean, sea, lake, or another river.
 
• It is formed by the **deposition of sediment** carried by the river as the flow velocity decreases upon entering the stagnant water.
 
• Deltas are typically fan-shaped or triangular, but their formation depends on the interaction between sediment supply, river flow, and tidal or wave action.
 
• **Famous examples** include the **Sundarbans Delta** (formed by the Ganges, Brahmaputra, and Meghna rivers) and the **Nile Delta**.
 
• Deltas support rich biodiversity and are crucial for agriculture, fisheries, and human settlements. They provide fertile soil due to the accumulation of sediments over time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lagoon:**

 
 
• A lagoon is a shallow body of water separated from a larger body of water, such as a sea, by barrier islands, reefs, or sandbanks.
 
• They are common in coastal areas and can be classified as coastal lagoons or atoll lagoons.
 
• Examples include the **Chilka Lake in India**, which is the largest coastal lagoon in the country.
 
 
 
• **Estuary:**
 
 
• An estuary is a partially enclosed coastal body of water where freshwater from rivers and streams mixes with saltwater from the ocean.
 
• Estuaries are highly productive ecosystems that support diverse marine life.
 
• The **Hooghly Estuary** in India is an example of an estuary.
 
 
 
• **Oxbow Lake:**
 
 
• An oxbow lake is a U-shaped body of water formed when a wide meander of a river is cut off from the main channel.
 
• It occurs when the river changes its course, leaving behind a standalone water body.
 
• Such lakes are found along floodplains and are a common feature of mature rivers.
 
 
 
• **Delta Formation:**
 
 
• The process of delta formation involves sediment deposition due to reduced velocity of a river as it enters stagnant water.
 
• Factors such as wave action, tides, and sediment composition determine the shape and type of the delta.
 
• Types of deltas include **arcuate deltas** (e.g., Nile Delta), **bird-foot deltas** (e.g., Mississippi Delta), and **cuspate deltas**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Deltas are vital for human settlements due to their fertile soil, which supports agriculture.
 
• The Sundarbans Delta is the largest delta in the world, formed by the Ganges and Brahmaputra rivers.
 
• Deltas also act as natural barriers against coastal erosion and floods.
 
• Many deltas face threats from rising sea levels and human activities such as dam construction and urbanization.

questions.question: In which part of India did the earliest iron objects appear in the overlap between the Neolithic and Megalithic phases?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**South India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The earliest **iron objects** in India appeared during the overlap between the **Neolithic** and **Megalithic phases**, primarily in **South India**.
 
• During the **Neolithic period**, people in South India were transitioning from stone tools to metal tools, marking the beginning of the use of iron in this region.
 
• The **Megalithic phase** in South India is characterized by the construction of large burial structures and the use of iron tools and weapons, indicating advancements in technology and societal development.
 
• Archaeological evidence from sites such as **Adichanallur**, **Hallur**, and **Brahmagiri** in South India shows the presence of iron objects and tools dating back to around **1200 BCE**.
 
• These iron objects were used for agricultural tools, weapons, and daily life implements, showing the importance of iron in early South Indian societies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Neolithic Period in India:**

 
 
• The Neolithic period in India dates back to around **6000 BCE**.
 
• It is characterized by the domestication of animals, agriculture, pottery-making, and the use of polished stone tools.
 
• Notable Neolithic sites include **Mehrgarh** (now in Pakistan), **Burzahom** (Kashmir), and **Kodekal** and **Hallur** (South India).
 
 
 
• **Megalithic Phase:**
 
 
• The Megalithic phase in India began around **1200 BCE** and is marked by the construction of large stone monuments or burial sites, known as megaliths.
 
• These monuments were often associated with iron tools and weapons, indicating the transition to the Iron Age.
 
• Megalithic sites in South India, such as **Adichanallur** and **Brahmagiri**, show evidence of complex burial practices and the use of iron tools.
 
 
 
• **Iron Age in India:**
 
 
• The Iron Age in India began around **1200 BCE** and marked significant technological advancements.
 
• Iron tools and weapons were widely used for agriculture, warfare, and daily activities.
 
• South India played a crucial role in the early adoption and development of iron metallurgy.
 
 
 
• **Archaeological Evidence:**
 
 
• Sites like **Adichanallur** have yielded iron implements such as sickles, swords, and axes.
 
• Excavations at **Hallur** have revealed early iron smelting techniques.
 
• These findings provide insights into the technological and cultural practices of early South Indian societies.
 
 
 
• **Important Points:**
 
 
• The overlap between the Neolithic and Megalithic phases in South India marks the transition from stone to iron tools.
 
• South India is considered one of the earliest regions in India to adopt iron technology.
 
• Iron objects from this period were used for practical and ceremonial purposes, highlighting their significance in early societies.

questions.question: CV Chandrasekhar, recipient of Padma Bhushan is a performer of which of the following classical dance forms of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatanatyam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **CV Chandrasekhar** is one of the most renowned exponents of **Bharatanatyam**, a classical dance form of India.
 
• He is a **recipient of the Padma Bhushan**, the third-highest civilian award in India, in recognition of his immense contribution to Indian classical dance.
 
• Bharatanatyam is a dance form that originated in **Tamil Nadu** and is known for its intricate footwork, graceful expressions, and emotive storytelling.
 
• CV Chandrasekhar is also an acclaimed **choreographer, teacher, and scholar** in the field of Bharatanatyam, having trained numerous students worldwide.
 
• He has played a significant role in preserving and propagating Bharatanatyam by combining its traditional roots with innovative choreography.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bharatanatyam:**

 
 
• **Origin:** Bharatanatyam originated in **temples of Tamil Nadu** as a form of devotional dance dedicated to the deities, particularly Lord Shiva.
 
• **Components:** The dance integrates **Bhava (expression), Raga (melody), Tala (rhythm), and Natya (dramatic art)**, collectively known as Bharatanatyam.
 
• **Features:** It is characterized by intricate hand gestures (Mudras), rhythmic footwork, elaborate costumes, and facial expressions that convey emotions and stories from Hindu mythology.
 
• **Performances:** Bharatanatyam performances often draw inspiration from texts like the **Natya Shastra** and include themes from the **Ramayana, Mahabharata, and Puranas**.
 
 
 
• **Other Classical Dance Forms of India:**
 
 
• **Mohiniattam:** Originating in **Kerala**, this dance form is known for its graceful, feminine movements and is often performed as a solo recital by women.
 
• **Kathakali:** A classical dance-drama also from **Kerala**, known for its elaborate costumes, face masks, and storytelling through music and dance.
 
• **Kathak:** Originating in **North India**, Kathak is characterized by its intricate footwork, spins, and storytelling through facial expressions and hand gestures.
 
 
 
• **Padma Bhushan Award:**
 
 
• It is the **third-highest civilian award** in India, instituted in **1954**, recognizing distinguished service of a high order in any field.
 
• Recipients include individuals from diverse fields such as art, science, public affairs, and sports.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Evolution of Bharatanatyam:**

 
 
• Historically, Bharatanatyam was performed in temples as a form of worship and was an integral part of religious rituals.
 
• In the 20th century, pioneers like **Rukmini Devi Arundale** redefined Bharatanatyam as a performance art, bringing it to the global stage.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Bharatanatyam:**
 
 
• It serves as a medium for spiritual expression and showcases Indian cultural heritage.
 
• It is one of the **eight recognized classical dance forms** of India as per the **Sangeet Natak Akademi**.

questions.question: Anil Srinivasan is one of the unique artists of India who plays which musical instrument?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Piano**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Anil Srinivasan** is a renowned Indian musician who is widely recognized for his exceptional skills in playing the **Piano**.
 
• He is known for blending Western classical piano music with Indian classical music, creating a unique and innovative musical style.
 
• Anil Srinivasan’s performances often involve collaborations with celebrated Indian classical artists, such as **Sikkil Gurucharan**, showcasing the harmonious fusion of diverse musical traditions.
 
• His contributions have earned him accolades and recognition both nationally and internationally, making him one of India’s most unique and versatile artists.
 
• Anil Srinivasan also uses music as a tool for education and therapy, working with schools and organizations to promote the cognitive and emotional benefits of music. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Piano:**

 
 
• The **Piano** is a musical instrument invented in the early 18th century by Bartolomeo Cristofori in Italy.
 
• It is widely used in various genres of music, including classical, jazz, pop, and rock, due to its versatility and dynamic range.
 
• The piano is played by pressing keys, which trigger hammers that strike strings inside the instrument, producing sound.
 
• Modern pianos come in two types: **grand pianos** and **upright pianos**, each suited to different settings and uses.
 
• Renowned pianists include **Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart**, **Ludwig van Beethoven**, and contemporary artists such as **Lang Lang**.
 
 
 
• **Other Musical Instruments:**
 
 
• **Flute:** A wind instrument made of wood or metal, played by blowing air across its opening. Famous flute players include **Hariprasad Chaurasia**.
 
• **Mandolin:** A string instrument popular in folk and classical music. It has a pear-shaped body and is played with a pick.
 
• **Violin:** A bowed string instrument used extensively in classical music. Renowned violinists include **Yehudi Menuhin** and **L. Subramaniam**.
 
 
 
• **Anil Srinivasan’s Contribution:**
 
 
• Anil Srinivasan has worked on innovative projects such as music education programs for children to enhance their learning abilities.
 
• He has collaborated with several organizations to use music as therapy for individuals with mental health challenges.
 
• His work bridges the gap between Indian classical music and Western styles, making music accessible to diverse audiences.

questions.question: The birdie (shuttlecock) of badminton is made up of 16 feathers, it is between 62-70 mm long and weighs between _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4.74 and 5.5 g**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **birdie (shuttlecock)** used in badminton is a high-quality projectile made with **16 feathers**, typically sourced from a goose or duck. 
 
• The shuttlecock has a standard length of **62-70 mm**, ensuring uniformity in play and compliance with international badminton regulations. 
 
• The official weight range of the shuttlecock is **4.74 to 5.5 grams**, as specified by the **Badminton World Federation (BWF)**. This weight ensures optimal flight stability and aerodynamics. 
 
• The feather structure of the shuttlecock provides precision in flight and is designed for high-speed gameplay. The unique design ensures it decelerates faster than most projectiles in sports. 
 
• The shuttlecock undergoes rigorous testing for weight and balance before being approved for professional matches, making the range of **4.74 to 5.5 grams** a critical specification.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Badminton Shuttlecock Design:**

 
 
• The shuttlecock consists of a **cork base**, typically covered with a thin layer of leather, which provides structural integrity and weight.
 
• The feathers are arranged in a circular pattern, glued to the cork base, and carefully trimmed to maintain balance and flight consistency.
 
• Most shuttlecocks used in professional tournaments are made of **goose feathers**, as they are more durable and provide better flight characteristics compared to synthetic ones.
 
• Modern shuttlecocks are tested for **speed, trajectory, and stability** under specific conditions to ensure compatibility with international standards.
 
 
 
• **Badminton World Federation (BWF) Regulations:**
 
 
• The **BWF** governs all aspects of badminton, including specifications for equipment such as shuttlecocks, rackets, and court dimensions.
 
• Shuttlecock weight and design are critical for maintaining fairness and uniform gameplay across tournaments worldwide.
 
• Shuttlecocks are categorized into different speeds (slow, medium, fast) to adapt to varying conditions like altitude and temperature during gameplay.
 
 
 
• **Feather Shuttlecock vs Synthetic Shuttlecock:**
 
 
• **Feather shuttlecocks** are preferred for professional play due to their precision and ability to decelerate quickly after being hit.
 
• **Synthetic shuttlecocks** are more durable and cost-effective but do not offer the same flight characteristics as feathered ones. They are commonly used in recreational play.
 
 
 
• **Important Facts about Badminton:**
 
 
• Badminton originated in **Pune, India**, during the British colonial era and was initially referred to as "Poona."
 
• The **first official badminton rules** were established in **1877** by the Bath Badminton Club in England.
 
• Badminton became an **Olympic sport** in **1992**, with events for singles, doubles, and mixed doubles.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Shuttlecock Testing:**

 
 
• Shuttlecock testing involves ensuring that it flies consistently through the air and lands within specific areas when hit with a standard force.
 
• The testing process includes verifying the weight, feather arrangement, and cork dimensions.
 
 
 
• **Professional Use:**
 
 
• Feathered shuttlecocks are exclusively used in **international tournaments** sanctioned by the BWF.
 
• Recreational players often use synthetic shuttlecocks to reduce costs and enhance durability.

questions.question: Nritya Chudamani Award is given every year by which cultural institution to an artist of Indian classical dance style?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sri Krishna Gana Sabha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nritya Chudamani Award** is one of the prestigious awards conferred annually by **Sri Krishna Gana Sabha**, a renowned cultural institution based in Chennai.
 
• This award is presented to an artist excelling in the field of **Indian classical dance styles**, such as Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Odissi, or other traditional dance forms.
 
• **Sri Krishna Gana Sabha** was established in **1953** and is dedicated to the promotion and celebration of Indian arts and culture, particularly dance and music.
 
• The award recognizes and honors the contribution of dancers who have made significant achievements and showcased excellence in their respective classical dance forms.
 
• The **Nritya Chudamani Award** is considered a mark of distinction and respect in the classical dance community, encouraging artists to preserve and promote India’s rich cultural heritage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sri Krishna Gana Sabha:**

 
 
• Sri Krishna Gana Sabha is one of the oldest and most reputed cultural organizations based in **Chennai, Tamil Nadu**.
 
• It has been instrumental in promoting Indian classical arts, including **dance, music, and drama**.
 
• The institution hosts several cultural events and festivals, such as the **Natya Kala Conference**, which attracts eminent artists and scholars globally.
 
• Sri Krishna Gana Sabha has been a platform for nurturing young talent and showcasing established performers in the field of Indian classical arts.
 
 
 
• **Indian Classical Dance Forms:**
 
 
• India has **8 classical dance forms**, recognized by the Sangeet Natak Akademi: Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Odissi, Manipuri, Kuchipudi, Mohiniyattam, Kathakali, and Sattriya.
 
• These dance forms are rooted in India's **rich cultural and spiritual traditions** and are often based on themes derived from Hindu mythology, epics, and devotional expressions.
 
• Bharatanatyam, for instance, is known for its intricate footwork and expressive hand gestures, while Kathak is famous for its storytelling elements and rhythmic patterns.
 
• Each dance form has its unique style, techniques, costumes, and musical accompaniment, representing the diversity of Indian art.
 
 
 
• **Other Prestigious Awards in Indian Classical Arts:**
 
 
• **Padma Awards:** India’s highest civilian honors, including Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Vibhushan, are often conferred on artists in the field of classical dance and music.
 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi Awards:** Recognized as the most prestigious honor for performing artists in India, these awards are presented annually by the Sangeet Natak Akademi.
 
• **Kalidas Samman:** Instituted by the Madhya Pradesh government, this award honors artists in classical music, dance, and theatre.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Cultural Institutions:**
 
 
• Cultural institutions like Sri Krishna Gana Sabha play a vital role in preserving and promoting India’s **cultural heritage**.
 
• They serve as platforms for artists to showcase their talent and connect with audiences who appreciate traditional art forms.
 
• Such institutions contribute to the continuity of classical arts and their relevance in modern times.
 
• They also play a significant role in fostering a sense of pride and identity among Indians regarding their **rich artistic traditions**.

questions.question: The ________ festival, in which the serpent goddess Mansa is worshipped, is celebrated in some parts of Bengal, Bihar and Jharkhand in India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihula**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bihula** is a traditional festival celebrated in parts of **Bengal, Bihar, and Jharkhand**, where the **serpent goddess Mansa** is worshipped.
 
• The festival is primarily associated with the **Bihula-Bishari folklore**, which emphasizes devotion, familial love, and the belief in resurrection.
 
• **Mansa Devi** is considered the goddess of snakes and fertility in Hindu mythology, particularly in eastern India.
 
• The rituals of Bihula include **folk songs, dance, and storytelling**, depicting the tale of Bihula's undeterred devotion to save her husband from death.
 
• The festival is celebrated during the monsoon season, as snakes are most active during this time, symbolizing nature's balance and agricultural fertility.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About Mansa Devi:**

 
 
• **Mansa Devi** is a Hindu goddess associated with snakes, fertility, and the prevention of snakebite-related calamities.
 
• She is particularly worshipped in the states of **Bengal, Bihar, Jharkhand, and Assam** during festivals like Bihula.
 
• Her temples are often located near water bodies, symbolizing the habitat of snakes.
 
 
 
• **Other Festivals Worshipping Mansa Devi:**
 
 
• Besides Bihula, **Nag Panchami** is another festival celebrated across India to honor snakes and Mansa Devi.
 
• During Nag Panchami, devotees offer milk, flowers, and prayers to snake idols or live snakes.
 
 
 
• **Folk Significance of Bihula:**
 
 
• The legend of **Bihula-Bishari** is a tale of marital devotion and resilience, where Bihula embarks on a journey to revive her deceased husband.
 
• This folklore is preserved through oral traditions, including **songs and performances** in rural communities.
 
 
 
• **Serpent Worship in India:**
 
 
• Snake worship is an ancient tradition in India, symbolizing **fertility, protection, and renewal**.
 
• It is rooted in agricultural societies where snakes were considered guardians of crops and water resources.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ambubasi Festival:**

 
 
• This is a significant festival in Assam, associated with the **Kamakhya Temple**, symbolizing fertility and the goddess's menstrual cycle.
 
• It is not related to snake worship or Mansa Devi.
 
 
 
• **Kumbh Mela:**
 
 
• This is a major Hindu pilgrimage and religious gathering held at four locations in India: **Haridwar, Allahabad, Nashik, and Ujjain.**
 
• The festival involves bathing in sacred rivers and is not connected to the worship of Mansa Devi.
 
 
 
• **Matasya Festival:**
 
 
• This is a cultural festival in Rajasthan, celebrating **traditional arts and crafts.**
 
• It has no connection to serpent worship.

questions.question: In which of the following states was the highest male literacy rate recorded as per census 2011?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As per the **Census 2011**, **Kerala** recorded the **highest male literacy rate** in India, which stood at **96.11%**.
 
• Kerala is renowned for its strong educational infrastructure and policy initiatives that have prioritized literacy and education over decades.
 
• The state has consistently been a top performer in literacy rates, not only for males but also for females, making it the most literate state in the country overall.

• **Comparison with Other States:**
 
 
• **Goa:** Known for its high literacy rate, but it stands lower compared to Kerala, with male literacy at **92.81%**.
 
• **Sikkim:** Has made progress in literacy, but its male literacy rate of **87.29%** is lower than Kerala's.
 
• **Mizoram:** A northeastern state with a commendable literacy rate, but male literacy stands at **93.35%**, still lower than Kerala.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Literacy:**
 
 
• Literacy is a critical factor in the **socio-economic development** of a region.
 
• It empowers individuals to access better employment opportunities, healthcare, and participate in civic activities.
 
• High literacy rates are often associated with **higher human development indices** and improved quality of life.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Census 2011:**

 
 
• The **2011 Census** was the 15th Indian Census and the 7th after independence.
 
• The census is conducted every 10 years to collect data on various population parameters, including literacy, population, and employment.
 
• It is conducted by the **Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner**, under the Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India.
 
 
 
• **Gender Gap in Literacy:**
 
 
• Despite progress, India still faces a **gender gap** in literacy rates, with male literacy significantly higher than female literacy.
 
• Efforts like the **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao** scheme aim to address these disparities.

questions.question: In which year did Henry Moseley use X-rays to measure the wavelength of elements, and correlate these measurements with their atomic numbers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1913**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Henry Moseley**, an English physicist, used **X-ray spectroscopy** in **1913** to measure the wavelengths of X-rays emitted by elements.
 
• Moseley discovered that these wavelengths were correlated with the **atomic number** of each element rather than their atomic weight.
 
• This groundbreaking work led to the modern understanding of the **periodic table**, reorganizing elements based on their atomic numbers rather than atomic masses.
 
• Moseley formulated the concept of **Moseley's Law**, which states that the square root of the frequency of emitted X-rays is proportional to the atomic number.
 
• This study established the **atomic number** as a fundamental property of elements, marking a significant advancement in atomic physics and chemistry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Henry Moseley’s Contributions:**

 
 
• Moseley’s work provided clarity in the arrangement of elements in the **periodic table**, identifying gaps where undiscovered elements should be placed.
 
• His research directly influenced the discovery of new elements such as **technetium (atomic number 43)** and **promethium (atomic number 61)**.
 
• Moseley’s findings resolved inconsistencies in the earlier classification, where elements like iodine and tellurium were misplaced due to reliance on atomic weights.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Moseley’s Law:**
 
 
• Moseley’s Law is used in **X-ray crystallography** to analyze the structure of materials and identify elements.
 
• It is widely employed in **scientific and industrial fields**, including material science and analytical chemistry.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• Moseley conducted his research during the early 20th century, a period marked by significant advancements in quantum physics and atomic theory.
 
• His work complemented the discoveries of other scientists like **Dmitri Mendeleev**, who initially proposed the periodic table based on atomic weights.
 
 
 
• **Important Points:**
 
 
• Moseley’s untimely death in **World War I** in 1915 at the age of 27 was a great loss to the scientific community.
 
• His contributions are remembered as a foundational step in the development of **modern atomic theory**.
 
• The atomic numbers identified by Moseley remain fundamental in **element classification** and periodic table organization.

questions.question: What was the primary effect of the Green Revolution on India’s agriculture?

options.text: Reduction in employment in the industrial sector

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Self-sufficiency in food grains**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Green Revolution** was introduced in India during the 1960s under the leadership of **Dr. M.S. Swaminathan**, often referred to as the "Father of the Green Revolution in India." It aimed at increasing agricultural productivity to combat food shortages.
 
• The primary effect of the Green Revolution was the achievement of **self-sufficiency in food grains**, particularly in crops like wheat and rice, ensuring that India no longer relied heavily on food imports to feed its population.
 
• The revolution involved the adoption of **high-yield variety (HYV) seeds**, improved irrigation techniques, modern agricultural machinery, and the extensive use of fertilizers and pesticides.
 
• States like **Punjab, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh** became the hub of agricultural growth, contributing significantly to India's increased production of food grains.
 
• While the Green Revolution ensured food security for the nation, it also had unintended consequences, such as environmental degradation, soil fertility depletion, and water resource overuse.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Key Features of the Green Revolution:**

 
 
• The Green Revolution introduced **high-yield variety (HYV) seeds** like IR8 rice and K68 wheat, which dramatically increased crop productivity.
 
• It emphasized the use of **chemical fertilizers, pesticides, and modern irrigation methods** to boost agricultural output.
 
• The revolution also encouraged the use of **mechanized tools** such as tractors and threshers to improve efficiency in farming.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Green Revolution:**
 
 
• **Positive Impact:** India achieved **self-sufficiency in food production**, particularly in wheat and rice, reducing dependence on food imports.
 
• It transformed India from a **food-deficit country** into a food exporter, boosting agricultural exports and generating rural employment.
 
• **Negative Impact:** Overuse of chemical fertilizers and pesticides led to **soil degradation, water table depletion, and environmental pollution**.
 
 
 
• **Role of Regions in the Green Revolution:**
 
 
• **Punjab, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh** were the primary beneficiaries, owing to their fertile lands and irrigation facilities.
 
• States with lesser access to irrigation and infrastructure, such as **Bihar and Odisha**, lagged behind, creating regional disparities in agricultural development.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Options:**
 
 
• **Option 1: Reduction in employment in the industrial sector:** The Green Revolution focused on agriculture, and its effects were unrelated to employment in the industrial sector. This statement is **incorrect**.
 
• **Option 2: Decline in food grain production:** The revolution led to an increase, not a decline, in food grain production. This statement is **incorrect**.
 
• **Option 4: Increased reliance on food imports:** The Green Revolution reduced reliance on imports by achieving self-sufficiency. This statement is **incorrect**.
 
 
 
• **Important Points:**
 
 
• The **Green Revolution** was a global agricultural movement, but its impact was especially significant in countries like India, Mexico, and the Philippines.
 
• It was supported by international organizations such as the **Ford Foundation** and **Rockefeller Foundation**.
 
• In India, the first phase of the Green Revolution focused on **wheat production**, and the second phase expanded to crops like rice and maize.

questions.question: Who was the prominent leader of the Deoband Movement, which aimed to preserve Islamic culture?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Muhammad Qasim Nanotavi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Muhammad Qasim Nanotavi** was a prominent Islamic scholar and a key leader of the **Deoband Movement**, which aimed to preserve Islamic teachings and culture amidst the challenges of British colonial rule in India.
 
• The **Deoband Movement** was initiated in **1866** with the establishment of the **Darul Uloom Deoband**, an Islamic seminary located in **Deoband, Uttar Pradesh**.
 
• Muhammad Qasim Nanotavi believed in promoting education based on Islamic principles and worked to counter the influence of Western culture and education introduced by colonial powers.
 
• The movement emphasized the study of **Quran**, **Hadith**, and Islamic jurisprudence while opposing British policies that were seen as detrimental to Islamic traditions.
 
• Nanotavi's efforts helped lay the foundation for a robust Islamic educational system in India, which continues to influence Islamic education globally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Deoband Movement:**

 
 
• The movement was founded with the establishment of the **Darul Uloom Deoband** in **1866**.
 
• The primary goal of the movement was to preserve **Islamic teachings** and counter the cultural and educational impact of British colonial rule.
 
• The curriculum at Darul Uloom Deoband focused on traditional Islamic education, including the study of the **Quran**, **Hadith**, and **Fiqh** (Islamic jurisprudence).
 
• Graduates from this seminary spread its teachings across India and abroad, influencing Islamic education systems worldwide.
 
 
 
• **Muhammad Qasim Nanotavi:**
 
 
• Born in **1833** in **Nanauta**, Uttar Pradesh, Nanotavi was a scholar of **Islamic theology** and a reformer.
 
• He played a vital role in the **Indian Rebellion of 1857**, opposing British colonial rule.
 
• Nanotavi’s vision for Islamic education was rooted in the idea of reviving the Islamic spirit and resisting Western influence.
 
• He passed away in **1880**, but his legacy lives on through the Deoband Movement and its institutions.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of Darul Uloom Deoband:**
 
 
• It is among the most respected Islamic seminaries globally, offering advanced studies in **Islamic theology**.
 
• It advocates for adherence to Islamic principles and promotes **Sufi traditions**.
 
• It also serves as a center for Islamic jurisprudence and fatwa issuance, catering to queries from across the world.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Leaders:**
 
 
• **Maulana Abul Kalam Azad:** He was a freedom fighter, scholar, and India’s first Education Minister, but not a leader of the Deoband Movement.
 
• **Syed Ahmed Khan:** He founded the Aligarh Movement, focusing on modernizing education for Muslims, distinct from the Deoband Movement.
 
• **Shah Waliullah:** He was an 18th-century reformer who significantly influenced Islamic thought in India but predated the Deoband Movement.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Deoband Movement** has been instrumental in shaping Islamic education and preserving Islamic traditions in South Asia.
 
• It has inspired the establishment of Islamic seminaries in several countries, including **Pakistan**, **Bangladesh**, and **South Africa**.
 
• The teachings of Muhammad Qasim Nanotavi and the principles of the Deoband Movement continue to influence Islamic scholars and institutions globally.
